newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas rallies, then slips back, ends slightly.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas rallies, then slips back, ends slightly.

text.p: UK spot natural gas prices ended the day slightly firmer on Tuesday after rallying in the morning and then slipping back and losing some of the gains in the afternoon, traders and brokers said.

One company bid the market higher in the morning and bought significant volumes in several periods. This company was seen by many players as largely responsible for the price rise, as several other participants looked to offload gas acquired relatively cheaply in the last two days.

But the buyer slowed down its activities after lunch, and the whole market slipped back slightly, dealers said. By the close most periods were still above the closing levels of Monday, but the early gains were not sustained.
The October gas year was heard bid at 12.35 pence a therm in the morning and offered at 12.50 pence, compared with a bid/offer spread of 12.25/12.35 pence by the close on Monday.

But the day's main buyer did not buy the whole year, preferring instead to buy individual quarters to make up a year strip. Other dealers said the average of the quarters bought by the buyer averaged out at 12.50 pence in any case.
Q1 saw the most interest of the day, with at least six trades seen, all of 25,000 therms a day, giving a total of 150,000 therms a day for the quarter.

But there was also good interest in the third and fourth quarters of this year. Q3 traded at least three times as a quarter, and there were also several individual deals done for July as well as at least one for September.
There was also good buying on the prompt market, with one buyer picking up 200,000 therms on the within day market and another 540,000 therms on the day ahead market.

The rise on the spot market was reflected on the IPE futures contract, where 85 lots traded in four deals. Prices were between 0.10 pence and 0.15 pence a therm higher than Monday's settlement levels. --Sebastian Alison, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 6412
